n: Nephi takes over again. Jacob said much more, but Nephi recorded only what he felt was enough.
Nephi introduces thirteen chapters of Isaiah. He loves Isaiah’s words and will apply them to his people, because Isaiah saw the Redeemer just as Nephi did.

f.w: I will liken his words unto my people

n: Jacob also saw Christ. Isaiah, Nephi, and Jacob are three witnesses, and God establishes His word through multiple witnesses.
Nephi delights in proving that Christ will come. The law of Moses and everything God has given since the beginning “typify” Him — they are symbols pointing to Christ.

f.g: Serving as a type — a symbol or foreshadowing.

n: He delights in God’s covenants, grace, justice, power, and mercy in the eternal plan of deliverance from death.

f.w: the great and eternal plan of deliverance

n: He delights in teaching that without Christ, all would perish.

f.w: save Christ should come all men must perish

n: If there were no Christ, there would be no God and no creation. But there is a God, and He is Christ, who will come at His appointed time. Nephi identifies the God of Israel with Christ.

f.w: there is a God, and he is Christ

n: Nephi now quotes Isaiah so his people may rejoice for all humanity. He invites readers to liken Isaiah’s words to themselves and all people.
